preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is between 1 and 2013 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(S) <= 2013 for S in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For every test case string S, its length is between 1 and 2013 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ?' for c in S) for S in test_cases)
preconditions.description: Every character in every test case string S is either a capital letter A-Z or a question mark.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(len(out) == len(inp) and all((c == '?' or out[i] == inp[i]) for i, c in enumerate(out)) for inp, out in zip(test_cases, output_lines))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output string has the same length as the input, and every non-question-mark character in the input is preserved in the output at the same position.

postconditions.expression: all(all(c in 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ' for c in out) for out in output_lines)
postconditions.description: Every character in every output string is a capital letter from A to Z.

postconditions.expression: all(count_chef(out) == max(count_chef(cand) for cand in candidates(inp)) for inp, out in zip(test_cases, output_lines))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output string achieves the maximum possible number of 'CHEF' substrings among all valid replacements of question marks.

postconditions.expression: all(out == min([cand for cand in candidates(inp) if count_chef(cand) == max(count_chef(c) for c in candidates(inp))]) for inp, out in zip(test_cases, output_lines))
postconditions.description: Among all valid strings that achieve the maximum number of 'CHEF' substrings, the output string is the lexicographically smallest one.
